claim: GWAS requires increasingly larger sample sizes to overcome statistical correction for multiple testing to uncover novel significant association signals (p<5×10−8).
source: To uncover novel significant association signals (p<5×10−8), genome-wide association studies (GWAS) requires increasingly larger sample sizes to overcome statistical correction for multiple testing.
evidence: This is a statement about the general requirements of GWAS methodology, drawing from established scientific understanding of multiple testing correction.

claim: Biological constraints using chromatin accessibility and direct contact with gene promoters can identify associations among suggestive signals (5 × 10−8≤p<5×10−4) in GWAS efforts.
source: As an alternative, we aimed to identify associations among suggestive signals (5 × 10−8≤p<5×10−4) in increasingly powered GWAS efforts using chromatin accessibility and direct contact with gene promoters as biological constraints.
evidence: This is the stated aim of the study, which is then tested through the described methodology.

claim: The biological constraint approach identified 15 loci at p<5×10−5 in the 2010 BMI GWAS.
source: This approach, with its extremely low false-positive rate, identified 15 loci at p<5×10−5 in the 2010 GWAS, of which 13 achieved genome-wide significance by 2018, including at NAV1, MTIF3, and ADCY3.
evidence: This is a direct report of the results from applying the method to the 2010 GWAS data.

claim: 13 of the 15 loci identified at p<5×10−5 in the 2010 BMI GWAS achieved genome-wide significance by 2018.
source: This approach, with its extremely low false-positive rate, identified 15 loci at p<5×10−5 in the 2010 GWAS, of which 13 achieved genome-wide significance by 2018, including at NAV1, MTIF3, and ADCY3.
evidence: This is a direct report of the validation results comparing 2010 predictions to 2018 GWAS outcomes.

claim: NAV1, MTIF3, and ADCY3 are among the loci that achieved genome-wide significance by 2018 after being identified in the 2010 GWAS at p<5×10−5.
source: This approach, with its extremely low false-positive rate, identified 15 loci at p<5×10−5 in the 2010 GWAS, of which 13 achieved genome-wide significance by 2018, including at NAV1, MTIF3, and ADCY3.
evidence: These are specific examples of loci that were validated in the 2018 GWAS.

claim: Eighty percent of constrained 2015 BMI loci achieved genome-wide significance in 2018.
source: Eighty percent of constrained 2015 loci achieved genome-wide significance in 2018.
evidence: This is a direct report of the validation rate for the 2015 to 2018 comparison.

claim: Similar results were observed in waist-to-hip ratio analyses.
source: We observed similar results in waist-to-hip ratio analyses.
evidence: This indicates that the method was also applied to WHR data with comparable outcomes.

claim: Biological constraints on sub-significant GWAS signals can reveal potentially true-positive loci for further investigation in existing data sets without increasing sample size.
source: In conclusion, biological constraints on sub-significant GWAS signals can reveal potentially true-positive loci for further investigation in existing data sets without increasing sample size.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from the study's findings.

claim: As of July 2020, the GWAS Catalog consisted of 4628 publications reporting a total of 189,811 associations that achieved genome-wide significance (p<5×10−8).
source: As of July 2020, the GWAS Catalog consisted of 4628 publications reporting a total of 189,811 associations that achieved genome-wide significance (p<5×10−8) between genetic variants and human common complex traits.
evidence: This is a factual statement about the GWAS Catalog contents at a specific time point.

claim: In 2009, 54 near-independent genome-wide significant signals associated with variation in height had been identified.
source: For instance, in 2009, 54 near-independent genome-wide significant (GWS) signals associated with variation in height had been identified in a population of tens of thousands of individuals (Visscher, 2008), while by 2014, that number had jumped to 697 and was estimated to explain more than 20% of the trait's heritability (Wood et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a historical fact about height GWAS supported by a citation.

claim: By 2014, 697 genome-wide significant signals associated with height had been identified, explaining more than 20% of the trait's heritability.
source: For instance, in 2009, 54 near-independent genome-wide significant (GWS) signals associated with variation in height had been identified in a population of tens of thousands of individuals (Visscher, 2008), while by 2014, that number had jumped to 697 and was estimated to explain more than 20% of the trait's heritability (Wood et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a historical fact about height GWAS supported by a citation.

claim: The number of significant GWS signals for height increased to 3,290 in 2018, accounting for nearly a quarter of the heritability.
source: The number of significant GWS signals increased to 3,290 in 2018, accounting for nearly a quarter of the heritability (Yengo et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a historical fact about height GWAS supported by a citation.

claim: A large proportion of predicted heritability remains unexplained despite a constantly growing number of implicated loci in GWAS.
source: And yet, despite these successes, GWAS has a clear shortcoming in that a large proportion of predicted heritability remains unexplained despite a constantly growing number of implicated loci (Tam et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a known limitation of GWAS supported by a citation.

claim: Novel loci in GWAS are only identifiable using larger sample sizes, which come at a significant cost of both time and money.
source: These novel loci are only identifiable using larger sample sizes, which come at a significant cost of both time and money, and each successive independent signal explains less and less of the overall estimated heritability (Zuk et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a statement about the practical limitations of GWAS supported by a citation.

claim: Each successive independent signal in GWAS explains less and less of the overall estimated heritability.
source: These novel loci are only identifiable using larger sample sizes, which come at a significant cost of both time and money, and each successive independent signal explains less and less of the overall estimated heritability (Zuk et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a known pattern in GWAS supported by a citation.

claim: Sub-threshold signals have been selected for replication in a stage 2 GWAS due to their proximity to putative candidate genes to identify novel loci.
source: Sub-threshold signals have been selected for replication in a stage 2 GWAS due to their proximity to putative candidate genes to identify novel loci, as with the identification of the obesity locus NPC1 and replicated subsequently in a large meta-analysis (Meyre et al., 2009; Turcot et al., 2018).
evidence: This describes a previous approach to handling sub-threshold signals, supported by citations.

claim: The obesity locus NPC1 was identified through selection of sub-threshold signals and replicated subsequently in a large meta-analysis.
source: Sub-threshold signals have been selected for replication in a stage 2 GWAS due to their proximity to putative candidate genes to identify novel loci, as with the identification of the obesity locus NPC1 and replicated subsequently in a large meta-analysis (Meyre et al., 2009; Turcot et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a specific example of successful sub-threshold signal identification supported by citations.

claim: Epigenomic maps have been utilized to implicate biologically relevant sub-threshold variants that were subsequently experimentally validated.
source: Epigenomic maps have also been utilized to implicate biologically relevant sub-threshold variants that were subsequently experimentally validated (Wang et al., 2016).
evidence: This describes another previous approach to handling sub-threshold signals, supported by a citation.

claim: RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, and high-resolution promoter-focused Capture C have been developed to facilitate the annotation of genes and their regulatory elements.
source: Over the past decade, sequencing technologies such aa RNA-seq (Wang et al., 2009), ATAC-seq (Buenrostro et al., 2013), and high-resolution promoter-focused Capture C Chesi et al., 2019; Hughes et al., 2014; Su et al., 2020 have been developed to facilitate the annotation of genes and their regulatory elements.
evidence: This is a statement about the development of sequencing technologies supported by citations.

claim: 3D genomics data have been utilized to identify physical variant-to-gene interactions to implicate effector genes at GWAS loci.
source: Such data have been utilized to identify physical variant-to-gene interactions via three-dimensional genomics to implicate effector genes at GWAS loci where both sequence variant and gene reside within regions of open chromatin (Arnold et al., 2015; Çalışkan et al., 2019; Chesi et al., 2019; Cousminer et al., 2020; Javierre et al., 2016; Smemo et al., 2014; Su et al., 2019; Su et al., 2020).
evidence: This describes the application of 3D genomics to GWAS, supported by multiple citations.

claim: High-resolution promoter-focused Capture C with ATAC-seq can physically connect putatively functional non-coding elements harboring disease-relevant SNPs to promoters of specific genes.
source: By leveraging high-resolution promoter-focused Capture C with ATAC-seq, it is possible to physically connect putatively functional non-coding elements, such as enhancers, harboring disease-relevant SNPs to promoters of specific genes thereby potentially mechanistically implicated in the SNP-associated phenotype.
evidence: This describes the capability of the combined methodology used in the study.

claim: BMI and WHRadjBMI have been the subject of particularly large GWAS efforts by the GIANT consortium.
source: We chose to test this method utilizing GWAS data sets for body mass index (BMI) and waist-to-hip ratio adjusted for BMI (WHRadjBMI) as initial traits because they have both been the subject of particularly large GWAS efforts by the GIANT consortium.
evidence: This is a justification for the choice of traits based on available data.

claim: Both BMI and WHRadjBMI have implicated a large number of loci and therefore provide optimal statistical power.
source: Additionally, both traits have implicated a large number of loci and therefore provide optimal statistical power for our purposes.
evidence: This is a justification for the choice of traits based on statistical considerations.

claim: Previous studies have implicated adipocytes and hypothalamic neurons in BMI-associated variants.
source: With respect to variant-to-gene mapping, we utilized our existing 3D genomic data sets for adipocytes as well as hypothalamic neurons as previous studies have implicated these cell types in BMI-associated variants (Locke et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a justification for the choice of cell types based on prior research, supported by a citation.

claim: 26,343 proxy SNPs were detected for the 2010 suggestive SNPs at 5×10−8≤p<5×10−4.
source: Here, we detected 26,343 proxy SNPs; however, some of these proxy signals were in LD with an already established genome-wide significant signal.
evidence: This is a direct report of the number of proxy SNPs identified in the analysis.

claim: After filtering, 23,197 proxy SNPs remained that were independent of genome-wide significant signals.
source: This filtering left a residual of 23,197 signals.
evidence: This is a direct report of the number of proxy SNPs after filtering.

claim: Three ATAC-seq libraries from adipocytes resulted in 2,225,635 peaks.
source: These resulted in 2,225,635 adipocyte peaks and 179,212 hypothalamic neuron peaks.
evidence: This is a direct report of the ATAC-seq data generated.

claim: ATAC-seq libraries from hypothalamic neurons resulted in 179,212 peaks.
source: These resulted in 2,225,635 adipocyte peaks and 179,212 hypothalamic neuron peaks.
evidence: This is a direct report of the ATAC-seq data generated.

claim: The adipose capture C libraries had an average of 1.4 billion reads per library.
source: The adipose capture C libraries had an average of 1.4 billion reads per adipose library, with an average of 41% valid read pairs and 89% capture efficiency.
evidence: This is a direct report of the sequencing data quality metrics.

claim: The adipose capture C libraries had an average of 41% valid read pairs and 89% capture efficiency.
source: The adipose capture C libraries had an average of 1.4 billion reads per adipose library, with an average of 41% valid read pairs and 89% capture efficiency.
evidence: This is a direct report of the sequencing data quality metrics.

claim: 258,882 short-distance interactions were identified at 1-fragment resolution using the CHiCAGO pipeline.
source: We then called significant interactions using the CHiCAGO pipeline and performed analyses at a 1-fragment resolution to identify short-distance interactions (258,882 interactions) and at 4-fragment resolution to identify long-distance interactions (278,040) (Cairns et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a direct report of the Capture C analysis results.

claim: 278,040 long-distance interactions were identified at 4-fragment resolution using the CHiCAGO pipeline.
source: We then called significant interactions using the CHiCAGO pipeline and performed analyses at a 1-fragment resolution to identify short-distance interactions (258,882 interactions) and at 4-fragment resolution to identify long-distance interactions (278,040) (Cairns et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a direct report of the Capture C analysis results.

claim: 161 of the 23,197 suggestive proxy SNPs survived biological filters at the most relaxed p-value threshold.
source: One hundred and sixty-one of the 23,197 suggestive proxy SNPs survived these biological filters at our most relaxed p-value threshold.
evidence: This is a direct report of the filtering results.

claim: The 161 surviving SNPs corresponded to 78 independent loci.
source: These SNPs corresponded to 78 loci, of which 11 achieved genome-wide significance by 2015 (Table 1); these are annotated on the 2015 BMI Manhattan plot (Figure 1).
evidence: This is a direct report of the number of independent loci identified.

claim: 11 of the 78 loci achieved genome-wide significance by 2015.
source: These SNPs corresponded to 78 loci, of which 11 achieved genome-wide significance by 2015 (Table 1); these are annotated on the 2015 BMI Manhattan plot (Figure 1).
evidence: This is a direct report of the validation results for 2010 to 2015.

claim: Four of the 11 loci that achieved GWS by 2015 were highlighted in the 2010 study but were only considered 'suggestive' within the stage one discovery set.
source: Four of these loci were highlighted in the 2010 study, but the associations were only considered 'suggestive' within the stage one discovery set at that time, that is at p>5×10−8.
evidence: This provides context about which loci were previously noted in the 2010 study.

claim: The positive predictive value was low through 2015, and the proportion of constrained signals achieving GWS did not differ significantly from unconstrained signals within the corresponding p-value bin.
source: Across all suggestive bins and cell types, the positive predictive value was low through 2015, and the proportion of constrained signals actually achieving genome-wide significance (GWS) did not differ significantly from the proportion of the unconstrained signals achieving GWS within the corresponding p-value bin (Figure 2).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the results shown in Figure 2.

claim: The low positive predictive value through 2015 is likely a function of the relatively modest increase in sample size (+89,428) between 2010 and 2015.
source: This is likely a function of the relatively modest increase in sample size (+89,428) between 2010 and 2015.
evidence: This is an interpretation of why the PPV was low in the 2010-2015 comparison.

claim: At the p-value threshold of 5×10−8≤p<5×10−5, 6/15 2010 biologically constrained loci were GWS in 2015.
source: At the relatively relaxed p-value threshold of 5×10−8≤p<5×10−5, we observed that 6/15 2010 biologically constrained loci were GWS in 2015, whereas 43/163 unconstrained loci were GWS by 2015.
evidence: This is a direct report of the results at a specific p-value threshold.

claim: At the p-value threshold of 5×10−8≤p<5×10−5, 43/163 unconstrained loci were GWS by 2015.
source: At the relatively relaxed p-value threshold of 5×10−8≤p<5×10−5, we observed that 6/15 2010 biologically constrained loci were GWS in 2015, whereas 43/163 unconstrained loci were GWS by 2015.
evidence: This is a direct report of the results for unconstrained loci at a specific p-value threshold.

claim: 45 of the 78 2010 biologically constrained loci achieved genome-wide significance by the 2018 BMI GWAS.
source: Here, we observed that 45 of the 78 2010 biologically constrained loci achieved genome-wide significance by 2018 at the most relaxed p-value threshold (Table 2).
evidence: This is a direct report of the validation results for 2010 to 2018.

claim: 86.7% (13/15) of biologically constrained loci identified at 5×10−8≤p<5×10−5 achieved genome-wide significance by 2018.
source: At this threshold, 86.7% (13/15) of biologically constrained loci identified achieved genome-wide significance by 2018, whereas only 40% (6/15) had achieved genome-wide significance by 2015 (Figure 2); clearly, this improvement is a function of relative cohort size.
evidence: This is a direct report of the positive predictive value at a specific threshold.

claim: The improvement in positive predictive value from 2015 to 2018 is a function of relative cohort size.
source: At this threshold, 86.7% (13/15) of biologically constrained loci identified achieved genome-wide significance by 2018, whereas only 40% (6/15) had achieved genome-wide significance by 2015 (Figure 2); clearly, this improvement is a function of relative cohort size.
evidence: This is an interpretation of why the PPV improved between 2015 and 2018.

claim: An increase was also observed with loci identified with no constraint (43/163 suggestive 2010 loci achieving GWS by 2015 and 105/163 achieving GWS by 2018).
source: While an increase was also observed with loci identified with no constraint (43/163 suggestive 2010 loci achieving GWS by 2015 and 105/163 achieving GWS by 2018), the precision was significantly higher with the biological constraint than without.
evidence: This is a direct report of the results for unconstrained loci across time points.

claim: The precision was significantly higher with the biological constraint than without.
source: While an increase was also observed with loci identified with no constraint (43/163 suggestive 2010 loci achieving GWS by 2015 and 105/163 achieving GWS by 2018), the precision was significantly higher with the biological constraint than without.
evidence: This is a comparison of the performance of constrained vs unconstrained approaches.

claim: There is no point across either cell type or p-value bin where randomly sampled SNPs outperform the chromatin-constrained approach.
source: As shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1, there is no point across either cell type or p-value bin where randomly sampled SNPs outperform the chromatin-constrained approach.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: 44 of 78 suggestive loci were identified in the 5×10−8≤p<5×10−4 bin, with a positive predictive value approximately 1.2-fold higher than random selection.
source: Forty-four of 78 suggestive loci were identified in the 5×10−8≤p<5×10−4 bin, with a positive predictive value approximately 1.2-fold higher than random selection.
evidence: This is a direct report of the results at a specific p-value threshold.

claim: Fewer novel chromatin-implicated loci were detected in the 5×10−8≤p<5×10−5 bin, though the positive predictive value was approximately 1.5-fold higher than random.
source: As anticipated, fewer novel chromatin-implicated loci were detected in the 5×10−8≤p<5×10−5 bin, though the positive predictive value was approximately 1.5-fold higher than random.
evidence: This is a direct report of the results at a more stringent p-value threshold.

claim: The chromatin-constrained approach consistently performs better than random within these serial data sets.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that this chromatin-constrained approach consistently performs better than random within these serial data sets, though there are diminishing returns as the p-value threshold is made increasingly less stringent.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion about the performance of the method.

claim: There are diminishing returns as the p-value threshold is made increasingly less stringent.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that this chromatin-constrained approach consistently performs better than random within these serial data sets, though there are diminishing returns as the p-value threshold is made increasingly less stringent.
evidence: This is an observation about the relationship between p-value threshold and method performance.

claim: Across all cell types with 5×10−8≤p<5×10−4, 117 of the implicated 184 loci from 2015 reached GWS in 2018.
source: We observed that across all cell types with 5×10−8≤p<5×10−4, 117 of the implicated 184 loci reached GWS in 2018.
evidence: This is a direct report of the validation results for 2015 to 2018.

claim: At the 5×10−8≤p<5×10−5 threshold, 80% (57/71) of the constrained 2015 implicated loci reached GWS in 2018.
source: At the 5×10−8≤p<5×10−5 threshold, 80% (57/71) of the constrained 2015 implicated loci reached GWS in 2018, while 59% (148/248) of the unconstrained 2015 loci reached GWS in 2018 (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a direct report of the positive predictive value at a specific threshold.

claim: 59% (148/248) of the unconstrained 2015 loci reached GWS in 2018.
source: At the 5×10−8≤p<5×10−5 threshold, 80% (57/71) of the constrained 2015 implicated loci reached GWS in 2018, while 59% (148/248) of the unconstrained 2015 loci reached GWS in 2018 (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a direct report of the results for unconstrained loci.

claim: At the 5×10−8≤p<5×10−6 threshold, 93% (26/28) of the surviving signals reached GWS by 2018 in both cell types.
source: Given the presence of many more loci in each bin, we observed significance at the 5×10−8≤p<5×10−6 threshold in both cell types, where 93% (26/28) of the surviving signals reached GWS by 2018 in both cell types.
evidence: This is a direct report of the positive predictive value at a more stringent threshold.

claim: The high PPV at 5×10−8≤p<5×10−6 is principally due to the larger sample sizes at this bin size relative to 2010.
source: This appears to be principally due to the larger sample sizes at this bin size relative to 2010, which provided additional power to observe such differences.
evidence: This is an interpretation of why the PPV was high at this threshold.

claim: This method positively identified sub-threshold BMI signals that went on to achieve GWS at a later date significantly more often than when no biological constraint is applied.
source: Considering the results of all BMI retrospective analyses through 2018, we found that this method positively identified sub-threshold BMI signals that went on to achieve GWS at a later date significantly more often than when we apply no biological constraint.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion about the overall performance of the method for BMI.

claim: 15,457 proxies were found within the most relaxed p-value threshold of 5×10−8≤p<5×10−4 for 2010 WHRadjBMI.
source: Here, we found 15,457 proxies within the most relaxed p-value threshold of 5×10−8≤p<5×10−4.
evidence: This is a direct report of the number of proxy SNPs identified for WHRadjBMI.

claim: 157 of the WHRadjBMI proxies survived biological constraints, corresponding to 71 independent loci.
source: One hundred and fifty-seven of these proxies survived our biological constraints, corresponding to 71 independent loci.
evidence: This is a direct report of the filtering results for WHRadjBMI.

claim: 36 of the 71 WHRadjBMI loci ultimately achieved GWS by the 2018 GWAS.
source: Thirty-six of these ultimately achieved GWS by the 2018 GWAS (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a direct report of the validation results for WHRadjBMI 2010 to 2018.

claim: Precision of the biologically constrained 2010 loci reaching genome-wide significance in 2018 for both traits through 5×10−8≤p<5×10−6 was 100% for each cell type, except for the 2010 WHRadjBMI SNPs constrained by adipose chromatin data which equals 83%.
source: Precision of the biologically constrained 2010 loci reaching genome-wide significance in 2018 for both traits through 5×10−8≤p<5×10−6 was 100% for each cell type, except for the 2010 WHRadjBMI SNPs constrained by adipose chromatin data which equals 83% (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct report of the precision values at a specific threshold.

claim: The precision at 5×10−8≤p<5×10−6 represents a 1.3- to 1.6-fold increase over the mean PPV of a randomly sampled unconstrained SNP set at the same p-value threshold.
source: This represents a 1.3- to 1.6-fold increase over the mean PPV of a randomly sampled unconstrained SNP set at the same p-value threshold.
evidence: This is a comparison of the constrained approach to random sampling.

claim: The chromatin-constraint surviving sub-threshold WHRadjBMI signals went on to achieve GWS at a later date significantly more often than when no constraint is applied.
source: Despite the larger rate of false positives at a threshold of 5×10−8<p<5×10−5 in WHRadjBMI relative to BMI, we still observe that the chromatin-constraint surviving sub-threshold WHRadjBMI signals went on to achieve GWS at a later date significantly more often than when we apply no constraint.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion about the overall performance of the method for WHRadjBMI.

claim: There was no p-value bin, cell type or trait for which there was a difference between the negative control set and the unconstrained set.
source: We found that there was no p-value bin, cell type or trait for which there was a difference between this negative set and the unconstrained set (Figure 7 and Figure 8).
evidence: This is a report of the negative control analysis results.

claim: The absence of observable differences between the negative control and unconstrained sets supports the inference that the differences observed between biological constrained data and unconstrained data are attributable to the chromatin-constrained analytic strategy.
source: The absence of observable differences between the negative control and unconstrained sets supports the inference that the differences observed between our biological constrained data and the unconstrained data are in fact attributable to the chromatin-constrained analytic strategy.
evidence: This is an interpretation of what the negative control results mean for the validity of the method.

claim: Across all thresholds and chromatin-constrained loci in each cell type, sensitivity was generally less than 25%.
source: We found that, across all thresholds and chromatin-constrained loci in each cell type, sensitivity was generally less than 25%, indicating a high rate of false negatives.
evidence: This is a report of the sensitivity metric for the method.

claim: The low sensitivity indicates a high rate of false negatives.
source: We found that, across all thresholds and chromatin-constrained loci in each cell type, sensitivity was generally less than 25%, indicating a high rate of false negatives.
evidence: This is an interpretation of what low sensitivity means.

claim: The low sensitivity is expected because the chromatin-constrained data represent effects that are only captured by the cell-types that were profiled.
source: This is expected because the chromatin-constrained data represent effects that are only captured by the cell-types (and their respective developmental maturities) that were profiled.
evidence: This is an explanation for why sensitivity is low.

claim: By combining the loci identified in either adipose or hypothalamic neurons, sensitivity was increased, though the increment was modest.
source: By combining the loci identified in either adipose or hypothalamic neurons, sensitivity was increased, though the increment was modest.
evidence: This is a report of the effect of combining cell types on sensitivity.

claim: Specificity was consistently >80%, and often >90%, indicating few false positives.
source: Specificity, however, was consistently >80%, and often >90%, indicating few false positives.
evidence: This is a report of the specificity metric for the method.

claim: The precision was particularly high through 5×10−8<p<5×10−5.
source: The precision was particularly high through 5×10−8<p<5×10−5; however, expanding through to 5×10−8<p<5×10−4 resulted in relatively high proportions of false positives in most analyses, although always at a lower rate than without a chromatin-constraint.
evidence: This is a report of the precision at different p-value thresholds.

claim: Expanding the threshold to 5×10−8<p<5×10−4 resulted in relatively high proportions of false positives in most analyses, although always at a lower rate than without a chromatin-constraint.
source: The precision was particularly high through 5×10−8<p<5×10−5; however, expanding through to 5×10−8<p<5×10−4 resulted in relatively high proportions of false positives in most analyses, although always at a lower rate than without a chromatin-constraint.
evidence: This is a report of the trade-off between threshold stringency and false positive rate.

claim: There was no instance across trait, cell type, or p-value bin in which the specificity of the negative control outperformed the variant-to-gene mapping filter.
source: There was no instance across trait, cell type, or p-value bin in which the specificity of the negative control outperformed the variant-to-gene mapping filter (Source data 1).
evidence: This is a report of the negative control analysis for specificity.

claim: The consistently high specificity and precision observed conveys the capacity of this chromatin-constraint to preferentially retain signals that are likely to achieve GWS in larger data sets while minimizing the presence of false positives through 5×10−8<p<5×10−5.
source: All together, the consistently high specificity and precision observed conveys the capacity of this chromatin-constraint to preferentially retain signals that are likely to achieve GWS in larger data sets while minimizing the presence of false positives through 5×10−8<p<5×10−5.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion about the performance characteristics of the method.

claim: The variant-to-gene structural mapping approach was recently described.
source: In this study, we used our recently described variant-to-gene structural mapping approach (Chesi et al., 2019; Su et al., 2020) to conduct retrospective biologically constrained analyses of previous sequential GWAS reports to determine whether we could implicate statistically suggestive SNPs that would subsequently achieve GWS in incrementally larger data sets.
evidence: This references prior work by the authors, supported by citations.

claim: The method enables the prioritization of statistically suggestive loci using a combination of high-resolution promoter-focused Capture C and ATAC-seq.
source: Using a combination of high-resolution promoter-focused Capture C and ATAC-seq, this method enables the prioritization of statistically suggestive loci.
evidence: This describes the capability of the method used in the study.

claim: The 2010 BMI GWAS had a sample size of N = 249,796.
source: Given the fairly modest increase in sample size between 2010 (N = 249,796) and 2015 (N = 339,224) for BMI, it was not particularly surprising that majority of the surviving 2010 BMI signals did not achieve GWS until 2018 (N = 681,275).
evidence: This is a factual statement about the sample size of the 2010 GWAS.

claim: The 2015 BMI GWAS had a sample size of N = 339,224.
source: Given the fairly modest increase in sample size between 2010 (N = 249,796) and 2015 (N = 339,224) for BMI, it was not particularly surprising that majority of the surviving 2010 BMI signals did not achieve GWS until 2018 (N = 681,275).
evidence: This is a factual statement about the sample size of the 2015 GWAS.

claim: The 2018 BMI GWAS had a sample size of N = 681,275.
source: Given the fairly modest increase in sample size between 2010 (N = 249,796) and 2015 (N = 339,224) for BMI, it was not particularly surprising that majority of the surviving 2010 BMI signals did not achieve GWS until 2018 (N = 681,275).
evidence: This is a factual statement about the sample size of the 2018 GWAS.

claim: Roughly 20% of the surviving 2010 signals achieved GWS by 2015 when reaching deeper into the 2010 suggestive signals through p<5×10−4.
source: Reaching deeper into the 2010 suggestive signals through p<5×10−4 showed a much clearer trend for both traits: roughly 20% of the surviving 2010 signals achieved GWS by 2015 and nearly 50% achieved GWS by 2018.
evidence: This is a report of the results at a more relaxed p-value threshold.

claim: Nearly 50% of the surviving 2010 signals achieved GWS by 2018 when reaching deeper into the 2010 suggestive signals through p<5×10−4.
source: Reaching deeper into the 2010 suggestive signals through p<5×10−4 showed a much clearer trend for both traits: roughly 20% of the surviving 2010 signals achieved GWS by 2015 and nearly 50% achieved GWS by 2018.
evidence: This is a report of the results at a more relaxed p-value threshold.

claim: The positive predictive value was nearly 90% for 2010 BMI constrained loci reaching GWS by 2018 at 5×10−8≤p<5×10−5.
source: While the positive predictive value was nearly 90% for 2010 BMI constrained loci reaching GWS by 2018 at 5×10−8≤p<5×10−5, only 65% of the surviving 2010 WHRadjBMI achieved GWS by the subsequent 2018 study.
evidence: This is a direct report of the PPV for BMI at a specific threshold.

claim: Only 65% of the surviving 2010 WHRadjBMI loci achieved GWS by the 2018 study at 5×10−8≤p<5×10−5.
source: While the positive predictive value was nearly 90% for 2010 BMI constrained loci reaching GWS by 2018 at 5×10−8≤p<5×10−5, only 65% of the surviving 2010 WHRadjBMI achieved GWS by the subsequent 2018 study.
evidence: This is a direct report of the PPV for WHRadjBMI at a specific threshold.

claim: At the threshold 5×10−8≤p<5×10−6, nearly all of the surviving loci for both traits reached GWS by their respective 2018 study, although the number of loci within this threshold is small (BMI: 4/4, WHRadjBMI: 5/6).
